problem:
Consider the matrix $B$ for which ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-3$ are eigenvalues, and

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$

are the respective eigenvectors. What are the values of $a,b,c$ given that

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}b & -3 \\ c & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}a & 0 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}b & -3 \\ c & 4\end{aligned}]}^{-1}?
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$ You're given that ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1$ are the eigenvalues of $A$, and
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$, ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are the respective eigenvectors. Find the matrices $P$ and $D$ such that $PD{P}^{-1}=A,$ where $D$ is a diagonal matrix.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the eigenvalues of the matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ we construct the diagonal matrix $D$ by writing the eigenvalues in the main diagonal:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, to construct the matrix $P,$ we simply write the respective eigenvectors as columns: 

- the $1$st column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-3,$ and

- the $2$nd column is the eigenvector corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$

Therefore, we get

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
